relevance_note: Case report of a woman with a clinical diagnosis of PAPA syndrome (in scope by diagnosis) but no PSTPIP1 variant: 'a female patient without PSTPIP1 mutations'.
method_note: Read the full text by hand; no table. The index patient has a clinical diagnosis of PAPA syndrome and is in scope by diagnosis, but the paper states 'PSTPIP1 gene mutation associated with familial PAPA syndrome was not observed', so there are no variant rows (no variant is tied to her). Two previously published pregnant PAPA patients from the Discussion are included because individual-level facts are given: 'ref 3 patient' (Hong et al.; woman, arthritis exacerbation at 31 weeks, IL-1 receptor antagonist) and 'ref 1 patient' (PG and acne worse during pregnancy; sex not stated). The reference list title of ref 3 says the Hong case had no identifiable CD2BP1 mutation; not used as a value. Ref 4 ('nonfamilial PAPA syndrome cases') gives no individual-level detail and gets no row. n_patients_reported left null: the paper gives no count of PSTPIP1-variant patients (its own patient had none). Age at diagnosis (30 years) is read from two adjacent sentences ('At age 30 years, she was suspected...' then 'a diagnosis of PAPA syndrome was made'). 'Her blood tests were all normal except...' is a whole-panel normal statement and was not used to exclude specific checklist items (anemia, cytopenias, inflammatory markers). One MRSA infection of the artificial joint was recorded as a feature but not as 'recurrent infections'. Vital status 'alive' is taken from the statement that she had completely recovered. Ages at onset are from 'joint inflammation that first appeared when she was 3 years old'; the sentence groups the skin lesions with it, so onset of PG/acne at 3 years is read from the same sentence. No contradictions found.
